what.text: This page follows refugees from Indonesia living in the United States, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 837 Indonesian refugees in the United States, 9.1% of all refugees from Indonesia.
Papua New Guinea hosts the most Indonesian refugees, followed by the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflicts in Indonesia over Aceh territory in 1990 and 1991 and from 1999 to 2005, and over East Timor territory in 1992 and 1997 to 1999.
It also records armed conflict over West Papua territory from 2018 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1995 at 6 refugees.
The figure was at its highest, 7845, at the end of 2008; the main years of displacement in the data are 2002 to 2003 and 2006 to 2013.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
These are year-end totals for the United States only, reported to UNHCR.
